faqs.question: What is a good short Diwali poem for a 4-year-old?
faqs.answer: Pick one with 4 to 6 lines about something the child can see, like a diya or a rangoli, and an action to go with it. NCERT's 2022 foundational framework expects children aged 3 to 8 to recite poems of about 4 to 5 sentences, so "Little Light" (4 lines) or "Dots at the Door" (6 lines) on this page fit that age.

faqs.question: How long should a Diwali poem be for a school recitation?
faqs.answer: For Classes 5 to 10, about 12 lines, which takes roughly 40 seconds at a slow stage pace. That is long enough to show expression and short enough to learn in under a week; the two recitation poems here are both 12 lines.

faqs.question: Can my child use these poems in a school competition?
faqs.answer: Yes, they were written for this page and are not copied from anywhere, but tell the teacher where the poem came from if the competition asks for original work. If it does, use one as a model and have the child write their own on the same 4-line shape.

faqs.question: Is there a famous English poem about Diwali?
faqs.answer: Sarojini Naidu's "Lakshmi, the Lotus-Born" is one of the few, and it is signed "Lakshmi Puja Day, 1915". It appears on pages 21 to 22 of her 1917 collection The Broken Wing, which is scanned on archive.org.

faqs.question: Can I print Sarojini Naidu's Lakshmi poem without permission?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Broken Wing was published in 1917 and Naidu died in 1949, so the poem is in the public domain in India and the United States; credit her and the book when you print it.

faqs.question: How can my child learn a Diwali poem by heart quickly?
faqs.answer: Practise it 3 to 4 times with actions on day one, then relearn it two days later instead of repeating it all in one sitting. A 2021 study of 87 students learning a song found spaced relearning, at two days or a week, beat a single massed session three weeks on.

faqs.question: When is Diwali in 2027?
faqs.answer: Lakshmi Puja, the main Diwali night, falls on Friday 29 October 2027. The five days run from Dhanteras on Wednesday 27 October to Bhai Dooj on Sunday 31 October.

faqs.question: What is a two-line Diwali poem in English called?
faqs.answer: A rhymed two-line poem is a couplet, and it is the easiest form to send because it fits one phone screen. This page has five, each for a different person, from a friend to a colleague.

faqs.question: How do I send a Diwali poem to someone who lives far away?
faqs.answer: Put it inside SubhSandesh's interactive Diwali card, where the letter in the shagun liffafa holds a longer poem and each wish diya can carry one line. It opens as a private link in any browser, so it works for a grandparent abroad as well as next door.

faqs.question: Should a children's Diwali poem mention firecrackers?
faqs.answer: It does not need to. Diyas, rangoli, sweets and the moonless night give children plenty to picture, and "Bruno's Diwali" on this page is about choosing a quieter celebration for a frightened pet.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Diwali Poem in English: 8 Originals for Kids and Recitation

A Diwali poem for a young child works best at 4 to 8 rhymed lines about one thing they can see, such as a diya, a rangoli or the moonless sky; a recitation piece runs about 12 lines, under a minute on stage. Every poem here is new, and short on purpose: 48.3% of pages shared on SubhSandesh are opened on a phone, where long verse means scrolling. People also leave it late: in our nearest festival analogue, Raksha Bandhan 2026 (n = 89 pages), 49.4% of greetings were made on the day itself.

Diwali 2027 falls on Friday 29 October. Below are eight poems, five couplets, a public-domain classic by Sarojini Naidu and a rehearsal plan.

## What makes a Diwali poem easy for a child to learn? NCERT's 4–5 line yardstick

A Diwali poem for children is a short rhymed verse a child can say from memory, with actions. NCERT's [National Curriculum Framework for the Foundational Stage (October 2022)](https://ncert.nic.in/pdf/NCF_for_Foundational_Stage_20_October_2022.pdf) expects children aged 3 to 8 to recite short poems of 4 to 5 sentences with gestures, and says every rhyme should be done at least 3 to 4 times.

Rhyme helps most when the line also makes sense. In a 1989 experiment reviewed by [Katz, Ando and Wiseheart (2021)](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC8665960), a rhyme cue alone recalled a target word with probability 0.192 and a meaning cue 0.142, but the two together 0.973. Each rhyme below is tied to a picture a child knows.

## Six short Diwali poems for kids, ages 3 to 10

Each lists length, read-aloud time and one action. Times are estimates at about 2 words a second.

### 1. "Little Light", ages 3 to 4

*4 lines, about 10 seconds. Cup both hands on line 3.*

> Clay cup, cotton wick,\
Oil poured slow, not quick.\
Cup your hands and hold it near:\
Little light, you're welcome here.

### 2. "Dots at the Door", ages 4 to 5

*6 lines, about 17 seconds. Count fingers on line 1.*

> One white dot, then two, then three,\
Didi draws a flower for me.\
Pink for petals, green for leaves,\
Orange where the border weaves.\
Step around it, mind your shoe:\
Someone special's walking through.

### 3. "The Moon's Night Off", ages 5 to 6

*8 lines, about 26 seconds. Point to each person named.*

> The moon is sleeping, out of sight;\
It's Amavasya, the darkest night.\
So Dadi lights the step outside,\
And Papa lights the window wide,\
And I light one beside my shoe,\
And baby claps, she's only two.\
Now count the lamps from roof to floor:\
We made a moon, and fifty more.

### 4. "Laddoo Delivery", ages 6 to 7

*6 lines, about 22 seconds. Dust off both knees at the end.*

> Twelve besan laddoos, round and neat,\
Four for each house along our street.\
Four to the Sharmas, four to the Gills,\
Three to the Mehtas on Pipal Hill.\
Mumma counts eleven, and then she sees\
One laddoo's worth of crumbs on my knees.

### 5. "Bruno's Diwali", ages 7 to 8

*8 lines, about 23 seconds. Peep from behind your hands on line 7.*

> Bruno hides beneath the bed\
When Diwali booms go overhead.\
So this year, on our balcony,\
We planned a quieter festivity:\
Forty diyas in one long row,\
A paper lantern, soft and slow,\
And Bruno, peeking, wags to say,\
"I like your Diwali best this way."

### 6. "Fourteen Years", ages 8 to 10

*8 lines, about 27 seconds. Sweep one arm wide on line 6.*

> Fourteen years in forest shade,\
Fourteen years of promises made;\
Then one bright morning came the word,\
The happiest news the town had heard.\
They swept each street, they lit each sill,\
They lined with lamps the furthest hill,\
So when he walked in through the gate,\
The dark had nowhere left to wait.

## Two Diwali poems for recitation, about 40 seconds each

They suit a school stage or the family puja. A 2025 review by [Tillmann, Goswami and Moghimi](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12915478) links children's beat-keeping to phonological and reading skills, so clap each poem's beat once before the first rehearsal.

### 7. "Before the First Diya", ages 10 to 12

*12 lines, about 39 seconds. Mime lifting a trunk lid on line 2.*

> A week before, the cleaning starts:\
Old trunks, old kites, old cricket charts,\
A postcard dated '98,\
A wind-up car without its plate.\
We scrub the brass until it shows\
My grinning face and Dadi's nose.\
Then comes the night. We light the sill,\
And all the swept-out house holds still.\
So when they ask what Diwali's for,\
I'll say it starts behind the door,\
In dusty boxes, opened, new;\
Then lamps come in, and so do you.

### 8. "What the Diya Said", ages 13 to 16

*12 lines, about 43 seconds. Stand still; let the last line land.*

> I was a lump of riverbank,\
Plain clay that no one thought to thank,\
Until a potter's wheel and hand\
Turned me to something small and planned.\
And on the moonless night of all\
You set me on a crumbling wall.\
I hold a thumb's worth, nothing more,\
But set me by the neighbour's door,\
And down the lane, and through the town,\
Till from the bridge you're looking down.\
So if you think one light is poor,\
Count us again. Then count some more.

## Five two-line Diwali poems in English, for a card or a message

A rhymed couplet fits one phone screen. Diwali 2027 runs five evenings, from Dhanteras on Wednesday 27 October to Bhai Dooj on Sunday 31 October.

- **For a friend:** "One diya for the year that's gone, one for the year to be, / And one for you, for always being there for me."
- **For family far away:** "Far apart this Diwali, the same flame in view: / I lit my diya at the hour you lit yours too."
- **For a brother or sister:** "Your rangoli's crooked and your laddoos are flat; / Happy Diwali anyway. I love you for that."
- **For an elder or a colleague:** "May Lakshmi find your door and choose to stay, / And may your worries take the night off, and the day."
- **For a quiet Diwali:** "No noise, no smoke, just a lamp on the sill: / A gentle Diwali, and every good wish still."

## Sarojini Naidu's "Lakshmi, the Lotus-Born" (Lakshmi Puja Day, 1915)

Sarojini Naidu wrote this for the festival itself, printing it in *The Broken Wing* (1917), pages 21 to 22, signed "Lakshmi Puja Day, 1915". The text is checked against the [1917 edition scanned on archive.org](https://archive.org/details/brokenwingsongso00nai) and is public domain.

> Thou who didst rise like a pearl from the ocean,\
Whose beauty surpasseth the splendour of morn!\
Lo! We invoke thee with eager devotion,\
Hearken, O Lotus-born!

> Come! with sweet eyelids and fingers caressing,\
With footfalls auspicious our thresholds adorn,\
And grant us the showers and the sheaves of thy blessing,\
Hearken, O Lotus-born!

> Prosper our cradles and kindred and cattle,\
And cherish our hearth-fires and coffers and corn,\
O watch o'er our seasons of peace and of battle,\
Hearken, O Lotus-born!

> For our dear Land do we offer oblation,\
O keep thou her glory unsullied, unshorn,\
And guard the invincible hope of our nation,\
Hearken, O Lotus-born!

The last stanza, a prayer for India from the independence years, suits an assembly. For younger children, the first two stanzas stand alone.

## Which Diwali poem to pick: length, time and audience compared

Four kinds of poem are compared below. SubhSandesh's phone figure sets the last column.

| Poem type | Lines | Read-aloud time (EST) | Best for | On a phone (48.3% of SubhSandesh pages open on one) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Couplet | 2 | 5–8 seconds | card, message | fits one screen |
| Kids' poem | 4–8 | 10–27 seconds | ages 3 to 10 | fits most screens |
| Recitation poem | 12 | about 40 seconds | ages 10 to 16, stage | scrolls; print it |
| Naidu classic | 16 | about 55 seconds | assembly, puja | scrolls; print it |

Anything over 8 lines belongs on paper or a stage. Send the short ones.

## How to rehearse a recitation poem before 29 October 2027

Space the practice out. In [Katz and colleagues' 2021 study](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC8665960), 87 university students recalled a two-verse song better three weeks later when relearning came two days or a week after first learning, not in the same sitting; two days worked as well as a week. They were adults learning a song, so this plan extrapolates.

- **Friday 22 October 2027:** say it 3 to 4 times with the actions, as NCERT suggests.
- **Sunday 24 October:** relearn it without the paper.
- **Wednesday 27 October:** one full run in front of the family.
- **Friday 29 October:** one run before the puja, then perform.

## Sending a Diwali poem to one person on SubhSandesh

SubhSandesh's [interactive Diwali card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-diwali) gives it a setting: the letter in a red-and-gold shagun liffafa can hold a recitation poem, and each wish diya lifts one line of a couplet or kids' poem. It takes about 5 minutes and opens as a private link in any browser, no app needed. Pages on the platform average 11.1 views each, so they get reopened.

To be heard rather than read, a [radio-style dedication page](https://subhsandesh.in/dedication) fits better: the recipient tunes to your station and hears your voice introduce a song, and that introduction can be the poem. It is not a Diwali template; keep it for a grandparent who would rather hear you.

## When a poem on a screen is the wrong choice

A link does nothing for a school recitation, where the teacher needs a printed copy. It also fails an elder without a smartphone; 51.7% of SubhSandesh page views happen off a phone, and a handwritten card often suits them better.

The Diwali page is built for one person, not a class of 40, so for a group, print the poem or post the couplet as text. A child who wants to write their own can borrow the 4-line shape of poem 1.

## Sources

- NCERT, *National Curriculum Framework for Foundational Stage*, 20 October 2022, section 4.4.4 and Box 4.4D.
- Katz, Ando and Wiseheart, *Cognitive Research: Principles and Implications*, 11 December 2021.
- Tillmann, Goswami and Moghimi, *Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences*, 16 December 2025.
- Naidu, *The Broken Wing*, 1917, pp. 21–22 (public domain).

structuralLimitations: SERP measured via DuckDuckGo HTML (India region, lower confidence than Google) plus one US-index WebSearch; Firecrawl unavailable. Pages were fetched with a plain HTTP client for headings/word count, not read in full prose.

No Diwali usage data exists; first-party lines are platform-wide (48.3% phone opens, 11.1 views/page) and the Raksha Bandhan 2026 analogue (n = 89), labelled as such in the body. The 51.7% off-phone figure is derived as 100 - 48.3.
Read-aloud times are estimates at ~2 words/second, labelled in the body; nothing was timed with children.

Katz et al. studied adults learning a song, not children learning poems; the rehearsal plan is labelled an extrapolation. The rhyme/meaning recall figures are Rubin & Wallace (1989) as reported in Katz et al.'s background, not a finding of Katz et al. themselves.

Naidu's poem is reproduced in full because it is a 1917 public-domain primary text (author d. 1949), the one classic the brief allows; archive.org OCR 'thyblessing' corrected to 'thy blessing', and the first refrain's '!' confirmed against a second scan where the first OCR showed '?'.

Storynory (US SERP) presents Naidu's 'Song of a Dream' as a Diwali poem; it is not about Diwali, so it was not used. Nazir Akbarabadi was avoided because b1 diwali-quotes and diwali-shayari already quote him.
Every poem and couplet line was 5-gram checked against all Diwali batch folders and strapi-live-articles.json (no poem-line hits) and 4-gram checked against five ranking poem pages (0 hits).
